answers: Whether to weep in the fifth month

easy.q: What did the messengers ask about?

medium.explanation: They spoke to “the priests” and “the prophets.”
medium.q: Whom did the messengers speak to about their question?

answers: The practice had continued for many years
The practice had already been forbidden

medium.q: What does “as I have done these so many years” show?

answers: To seek the LORD’s favor and guidance
medium.explanation: The messengers came before the LORD to seek an answer.
medium.q: What does “to pray before the LORD” mean in this passage?

answers: They asked whether to continue a practice they had kept
They asked about the king’s name
They asked for a description of Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: They were asking whether they should continue their established practice.
challenge.q: Why was the question about the fast a practical question rather than merely theoretical?

answers: It was a religious question requiring the word of the LORD
It was a matter of trade
It was a request for a government appointment

challenge.q: What does the arrival of the question before Zechariah suggest?

answers: Messengers came to the house of God, asked about fasting, and received the word of the LORD
A war began, cities were destroyed, and the temple was rebuilt
The people ate, drank, and stopped praying

paragraphs.title: Fasting Is Not the Main Point

easy.explanation: The passage says, “even those seventy years.”
easy.q: How long had the people fasted and mourned?

easy.explanation: The fifth and seventh months are named.
easy.q: In which months did they fast?

easy.explanation: The LORD asks whether they ate and drank “for yourselves.”
easy.q: For whom did the people eat and drink?

answers: Whether they truly fasted unto Him
Whether they fasted for one day
Whether only priests were allowed to fast
medium.explanation: He asks, “did ye at all fast unto me, even to me?”
medium.q: What was the LORD’s main question about their fasting?

medium.explanation: To mourn is to express sorrow, often with weeping.
medium.q: What does “mourned” mean in this context?

answers: The words of the former prophets
medium.explanation: He asks whether they should hear the words cried by the former prophets.
medium.q: What did the LORD say the people should hear?

answers: Their fasting may not have been truly devoted to the LORD
Their fasting was physically too long
Their fasting occurred in the wrong month only
challenge.explanation: The question examines whether the fasting was actually for the LORD.
challenge.q: What criticism is implied by the question, “did ye at all fast unto me”?

answers: They show that outward actions must be examined for their purpose
They prove that eating is always forbidden
They describe only the priests’ duties
challenge.explanation: The LORD contrasts fasting with eating and asks whose benefit was being sought.
challenge.q: How do eating and drinking support the passage’s message about fasting?

answers: Their words gave more important guidance than ritual alone
They were traveling through the land
They named the months of the year
challenge.explanation: The LORD directs the people back to the earlier prophetic message.
challenge.q: Why are the former prophets mentioned in connection with fasting?

paragraphs.title: Justice, Compassion, and Protection of the Vulnerable

easy.q: What kind of judgment were the people commanded to execute?

easy.explanation: They were to show “mercy and compassions.”
easy.q: What were people to show every man to his brother?

answers: The widow, the fatherless, the stranger, and the poor
easy.explanation: All four vulnerable groups are named in verse 10.
easy.q: Whom were the people forbidden to oppress?

answers: Both describe righteous treatment of other people
They are two names for fasting
They concern only the temple building
medium.explanation: The passage joins justice with mercy and compassion.
medium.q: How are true judgment and compassion related in these verses?

answers: To mistreat or take advantage of someone
To invite someone to a feast
medium.explanation: Oppression is harmful or unjust treatment.
medium.q: What does “oppress” mean in this passage?

answers: Imagine evil against their brother in their heart

medium.q: What additional evil were the people forbidden to do?

They were the leaders of the nation
They were responsible for the fasts
challenge.explanation: The list identifies people who could easily be mistreated or left without protection.
challenge.q: What does the list of the widow, the fatherless, the stranger, and the poor emphasize?

It removes the need for justice
It concerns thoughts about food only
challenge.explanation: The command reaches beyond actions to the heart.
challenge.q: How does the command about imagining evil relate to justice and compassion?

Prefer fasting above every other duty

paragraphs.title: Refusal to Listen and Its Consequences

easy.explanation: The passage says, “they refused to hearken.”
easy.q: How did the people respond to the prophets’ words?

answers: They made them as an adamant stone
easy.explanation: Their hearts were made “as an adamant stone.”
easy.q: What did the people do to their hearts?

easy.explanation: The land was made desolate after them.

answers: The end of the prophets’ words
medium.explanation: The passage says, “therefore came a great wrath from the LORD.”
medium.q: What resulted from the people’s refusal to listen?

answers: A rebellious refusal to accept correction
medium.explanation: The phrase pictures people turning away from obedience.
medium.q: What does “pulled away the shoulder” describe?

answers: They would not hear Him, and He would not hear them
They listened, and He remained silent
medium.explanation: The LORD says, “as he cried, and they would not hear; so they cried, and I would not hear.”
medium.q: What matching response between the people and the LORD is described?

answers: Refusal to listen led to wrath, scattering, and desolation
Eating led to peace in the land
challenge.explanation: The verses connect disobedience with divine wrath and national ruin.
challenge.q: What is the main cause-and-effect sequence in these verses?

answers: The people became hard and unwilling to hear God’s law
challenge.explanation: The image emphasizes hardness and resistance to God’s message.
challenge.q: What does the image of hearts becoming “an adamant stone” suggest?

answers: The pleasant land became desolate after them
challenge.explanation: The LORD says He scattered them and made the land desolate.
challenge.q: What happened when the people were scattered among the nations?
